about: Does charging overnight ruin your battery? Factory #32, backlog row 36, slug overnightcharge. One hard idea: two things speed up battery wear, heat and long hours at 100%; overnight, your phone handles the hours itself (Apple Optimized Battery Charging, Pixel Adaptive Charging, Samsung Adaptive battery protection can hold at 80% and finish right before you usually unplug), and you handle the heat (not under a pillow, out of a hot case). Hero: the bedside charge column with its 80 peg, plus the pillow pass/fail. Sources (read 2026-11-15) in BRIEF.md section 3. Planned silences: 0.5 s after the hook (frame-0 hit), 0.6 s after 'for good.' (dip: thermometer peaks), 0.5 s after 'just stop.' (fill clunks onto the 80 peg), 1.2 s after 'unplug.' (hero: alarm, fill to 100, screenshot hold). Narration-led: record the voice first and key every visual beat to its word times; re-chain `at` to the real Ming takes.

lines.text: Your phone doesn't charge all night.
So does charging overnight ruin your battery?
Two things speed up wear: heat, and hours at full charge.
But under a pillow, that heat gets trapped.
And heat can damage a battery for good.
Charge it in the open, out of a hot case.
Now watch: 11 at night, plugged in.
lines.say: Now watch. Eleven at night, plugged in.

lines.text: At 80 percent, it can just stop.
lines.say: At eighty percent, it can just stop.

lines.text: So it fills up right before you unplug.
Is your phone set to wait? Yes or no.
